answers.rationale: I'm a pragmatic developer who values transparency in code changes. Inline diffs would give me the visibility I need to catch issues before they hit production. The ability to review before accepting is exactly what would make me comfortable using this feature.

Checkpoint rollback is a game-changer for me. Knowing I can undo autonomous changes without manually reverting code gives me the safety net I need to trust an agent with complex refactoring or multi-file edits. This is the feature that tips the scale from skeptical to willing.

My biggest worry is that the agent might make subtle logic errors or introduce bugs that pass initial review but break at runtime. Even with good diffs, I could miss semantic issues that only show up in production.

answers.value: Refactoring variable names and imports across a well-tested module with comprehensive unit tests
answers.rationale: I'd start with low-risk refactoring tasks where the impact is mechanical and easy to verify. Renaming variables and reorganizing imports are changes where the test suite would immediately catch errors, giving me confidence before moving to more complex autonomous work.
